newsitem.title: USA: Russian palladium supply talk hits NYMEX palladium.
newsitem.headline: Russian palladium supply talk hits NYMEX palladium.

text.p: NYMEX palladium futures prices were sharply lower Wednesday, after seeing new contract highs Tuesday, on reports Russian palladium supplies to Japan may resume before the end of March.
But an official at the U.S. branch of Russia's metal export agency, Almaz, told Reuters Wednesday he was unable to confirm reports of a resumption of palladium supplies.
"I've just been in touch with Moscow about the question of supplies and they said such talk was very strange," Almaz spokesman Max Belov told Reuters.
"All we know is that the decree is still on Prime Minister Chernomyrdin's desk and we are unaware of any official news about palladium supplies resuming."

Last month an Almaz official in Tokyo said there would be no Russian supplies of palladium to Japan in March and supplies were unlikely in April also. He also said Russian expected to ship less palladium this year.
NYMEX June palladium was down $6.25 an ounce at $155.00 an ounce early Wednesday, after seeing a new contract high at $161.25 Tuesday.
Last December talks on a renewal of the Russian/Japanese supply contract broke down.
Meanwhile workers at Russia's Norilsk plant have threatened to strike over pay arrears later this month.
Russia accounts for about 60 percent of world supplies of palladium with most coming from the Norilsk plant and Russian stockpiles.
Russian stockpiles of palladium are a state secret but are currently estimated by some analysts to be around two million ounces.
